title: AI Tools
lede: N.I.N.A. Polaris ships a full suite of AI-powered image processing tools that run entirely on your local hardware. No cloud, no subscriptions, no data leaving your device. From background removal to super-resolution, every tool is available directly in the browser-based interface.

glance.label: 10 tools
glance.text: covering background extraction, denoising, deconvolution, star removal, halo removal, and super-resolution upscaling

glance.label: 4 backends
glance.text: browser GPU (WebGPU/WebGL), OpenCL, RKNN NPU (Rockchip RK3588), and Qualcomm QAIRT/QNN

glance.label: 100% local
glance.text: all inference runs on your device; models are cached in IndexedDB after the first download

glance.label: 4 precisions
glance.text: fp32, fp16, int16, and int8 (Quantization-Aware Training) for a range of speed/size trade-offs

tools.title: Background Gradient Extraction
tools.intro: Removes light-pollution gradients, vignetting, and uneven sky glow from linear frames. The neural network predicts the background plane itself rather than the corrected image, which is then subtracted or divided from the frame. The model sees the full frame at 256x256 for global context, then the predicted gradient is upscaled back to native resolution.

items.label: Global context:
items.text: downsampled to 256x256 so the model sees the whole frame in one pass, avoiding tile seams in the background estimate

items.label: Safe for nebulosity:
items.text: trained to distinguish smooth gradients from astronomical signal; faint nebulae and extended objects are preserved

items.label: Subtraction or division:
items.text: division mode handles multiplicative vignetting; subtraction mode handles additive gradients

items.label: Models:
items.text: GraXpert BGE compatible (v1, v2). Polaris BGE model in training

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab, AI Tools toolbar, and the image Editor

tools.title: AI Denoise
tools.intro: Removes sensor noise (shot noise, read noise, thermal noise) while preserving fine astronomical detail. Two GraXpert model variants are available: v2 (faster, lighter) and v3 (higher quality). Processing is tiled at 256x256 with cosine-feathered blending to eliminate boundary artefacts.

items.label: Tiled 256x256:
items.text: images of any size are processed in overlapping patches; borders are feathered so no tile seam is visible in the output

items.label: v2 vs v3:
items.text: v2 is the lighter model suitable for slower hardware; v3 has higher capacity and better preserves fine star spikes and faint detail

items.label: Color and mono:
items.text: both RGB and single-channel FITS are supported; the pipeline handles the channel layout automatically

items.label: Linear and stretched:
items.text: works at both stages; best results on linear calibrated masters before stretching

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab, AI Tools toolbar, and the image Editor

tools.title: AI Deconvolution: Stars
tools.intro: Sharpens point sources (stars) blurred by atmosphere, tracking error, or optical diffraction using a GraXpert neural network trained specifically on star fields. Produces tight, round stars without the ringing artefacts common in classical approaches.

items.label: Star-focused:
items.text: the model is trained to sharpen compact point sources; it understands that stars should be round and not produce halos

items.label: Complements the Objects model:
items.text: run Stars first, then Objects to sharpen both point sources and extended structure

items.label: Tiled 256x256:
items.text: feathered overlap blending; safe on full-resolution masters

items.label: Before/after slider:
items.text: inline comparison slider in the UI lets you judge the effect before saving

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab and AI Tools toolbar, under AI Sharpen

tools.title: AI Deconvolution: Objects
tools.intro: Sharpens extended objects such as galaxies, nebulae, and clusters. The GraXpert Objects model is optimized for spatially extended structure rather than point sources, recovering fine detail in galaxy arms, dust lanes, and emission regions.

items.label: Extended structure:
items.text: trained on galaxy and nebula images to sharpen fine structural detail without over-sharpening smooth emission regions

items.label: Pair with Stars:
items.text: for full-image processing, run the Objects model after the Stars model; each complements the other

items.label: Tiled 256x256:
items.text: feathered overlap blending; no tile seams in the output

items.label: Strength control:
items.text: adjustable strength slider (0.1 to 1.0) lets you dial in the effect

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab and AI Tools toolbar, under AI Sharpen

tools.title: Classical RL Deconvolution
tools.intro: Richardson-Lucy deconvolution driven by a PSF measured directly from the stars in the frame. The algorithm reverses the blurring introduced by atmosphere, tracking, and optics using the actual optical response of the imaging system rather than a generic neural network.

items.label: Measured PSF:
items.text: Moffat profile fit to real stars in the frame extracts FWHM, eccentricity, and orientation; the PSF is specific to that capture session

items.label: White 1994 damping:
items.text: corrections are gated by a per-pixel noise model; low-SNR regions are left untouched, preventing noise amplification

items.label: Photon-transfer noise model:
items.text: sigma is estimated from the frame itself using a shot + read noise model (sigma = sqrt(A*S + B)); no calibration input needed

items.label: Star protection:
items.text: a feathered mask around detected stars composites original star cores back after deconvolution, preventing ringing at bright sources

items.label: FWHM and star stats:
items.text: FWHM in pixels, eccentricity, and number of stars used are reported after each run

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab under AI Sharpen, Classical RL option

tools.title: Field Deconvolution
tools.intro: Extends Classical RL to handle field curvature, coma, and tilt: the PSF is measured independently in a configurable grid of tiles across the frame. Each tile gets its own PSF, and the results are blended with cosine feathering. Ideal for wide-field imagers where star shapes change from center to corner.

items.label: Per-tile PSF:
items.text: Moffat profiles fitted in each grid cell independently; a corner affected by coma uses a different kernel than the center

items.label: Configurable grid:
items.text: 2x2 to 8x8 tiles; more tiles give finer spatial correction at the cost of longer measurement time

items.label: Feathered blending:
items.text: cosine blend between adjacent PSF regions; the transition is invisible in the final image

items.label: Fallback:
items.text: tiles with too few stars fall back to the nearest measured PSF, so the whole frame is always processed

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab under AI Sharpen, Field RL option

tools.title: Browser RL Deconvolution
tools.intro: A new mode where the server measures the PSF and noise model (typically 5 to 15 seconds), returns a compact JSON payload, and the browser runs the heavy Richardson-Lucy iteration loop entirely in JavaScript. The SBC server CPU stays free for guiding, sequencing, and capture during the job.

items.label: Server does the science:
items.text: PSF extraction, noise model fit, and star detection all run server-side; these are fast and CPU-light

items.label: Browser does the work:
items.text: a pure-JavaScript FFT engine (radix-2 Cooley-Tukey) runs 512x512 tiled overlap-save RL iterations in the browser

items.label: Real-time progress:
items.text: a progress bar updates after each iteration; you can see the image sharpen live in the before/after slider

items.label: Same algorithm:
items.text: identical White 1994 damped RL, star protection, and noise gating as the server-side version

items.label: Enable it:
items.text: in the AI Sharpen modal, check the 'Run in browser' checkbox (global RL mode only; field mode stays server-side)

tools.title: Star Removal
tools.intro: Removes stars from the image while preserving all nebulosity for narrowband or starless processing workflows. Uses StarNet ONNX v1, converted from the original TensorFlow model, with full arm64 compatibility (unlike StarNet v2 which is x86-only).

items.label: Starless output:
items.text: all point sources are removed; extended emission, reflection nebulae, and galaxy structure are preserved

items.label: arm64 compatible:
items.text: StarNet v1 ONNX runs on Raspberry Pi, Orange Pi, and Radxa boards; v2 is excluded because it is an x86-only binary

items.label: Blend-back control:
items.text: after removal, the original stars can be blended back at any opacity for a final composition with softened stars

items.label: RGB and mono:
items.text: color and single-channel frames are both supported

items.label: Where:
items.text: FILES tab and AI Tools toolbar, Remove Stars option

tools.title: Halo Removal
tools.intro: Polaris's own neural network, trained from scratch on real astrophotos, removes the diffraction halo rings that appear around bright stars in fast refractors and Newtonians. Unlike classical approaches, the model understands the spatial context of each star and avoids removing genuine nebulosity near bright sources.

items.label: Polaris-native model:
items.text: trained on our own dataset of real astrophotos with synthetic halo augmentation; not a GraXpert repackage

items.label: Context-aware:
items.text: RGB 3-channel input gives the model enough context to distinguish halos from nearby nebulosity and emission regions

items.label: Evaluated at 50+ dB PSNR:
items.text: fp16 variant is essentially lossless vs fp32; int16 is within 0.03 dB

items.label: Four precisions:
items.text: fp32 (reference), fp16 (recommended), int16 (NPU/PTQ), int8 with QAT for maximum compression

items.label: Where:
items.text: AI Tools toolbar and the Editor's AI section, Halo Removal option

tools.title: AI Upscaling
tools.intro: Super-resolution 2x upscaling using Polaris's own UpscaleNet, a residual U-Net architecture trained on real astrophotos and designed for NPU-friendly int8 quantization. Useful for preparing images for large prints, high-DPI displays, or recovering more detail at the pixel level.

items.label: Polaris UpscaleNet:
items.text: custom residual U-Net; internally 2x-upsamples before the encoder, so the network processes the full high-resolution feature space

items.label: Evaluated at 50.22 dB PSNR:
items.text: fp16 (50.22 dB) is indistinguishable from fp32 (50.21 dB); int16 within 0.03 dB

items.label: int8 via QAT:
items.text: Quantization-Aware Training brings int8 back to near-lossless after PTQ showed a 3.3 dB degradation

items.label: 2x scale:
items.text: output is double the input dimensions in both axes; a 3000x2000 frame becomes 6000x4000

items.label: Where:
items.text: AI Tools toolbar and the Editor's AI section, Upscale option

backendsLede: Polaris automatically selects the best available inference backend for your hardware. Models are downloaded once and cached; the backend probe runs at startup and can be overridden in Settings.

backends.title: ORT Web (Browser GPU)
backends.intro: ONNX Runtime Web runs models directly in your browser using the GPU on your viewing device, keeping the SBC server CPU free. WebGPU is selected first (requires HTTPS), falling back to WebGL on HTTP or older browsers.

items.label: Zero server load:
items.text: inference runs entirely in the browser; the server only serves the model file once

items.label: IndexedDB cache:
items.text: models are stored in browser storage after the first download; subsequent runs are instant even offline

items.label: fp16 native:
items.text: GPU shaders run fp16 at full speed; WebGPU also supports fp32 for reference

items.label: HTTPS for WebGPU:
items.text: WebGPU requires a secure context; Polaris includes a self-signed certificate for LAN use

backends.title: OpenCL (SBC GPU)
backends.intro: The server-side GPU accelerates compute-heavy pixel operations (stacking, alignment, normalization) via OpenCL. Works on Adreno, Mali, PowerVR, and other OpenCL 1.2+ GPUs common in ARM SBCs. Automatic probe with CPU fallback.

items.label: Pixel math:
items.text: stacking (sigma-clip, kappa, mean), star alignment, per-pixel normalization all run on the GPU

items.label: Auto-probe:
items.text: Polaris tests the GPU at startup; if the probe fails it silently falls back to CPU

items.label: Silk.NET binding:
items.text: cross-platform P/Invoke via Silk.NET.OpenCL; no vendor SDK required

items.label: Toggle:
items.text: enable or disable in Settings; benchmark shows GPU vs CPU throughput on your hardware

backends.title: RKNN / NPU
backends.intro: The Neural Processing Unit in Rockchip RK3588 SoCs (Orange Pi 5 Pro, Radxa Rock 5, and others) runs ONNX models at 5x the CPU speed via the RKNN runtime. Models are converted to RKNN format with optional INT8 quantization.

items.label: 5x speedup:
items.text: measured 91 ms vs 457 ms per BGE/denoise tile vs CPU on RK3588

items.label: RKNN conversion:
items.text: a bundled conversion script turns ONNX fp16/int8 models into .rknn format; the runtime loads them transparently

items.label: INT8 support:
items.text: RKNN do_quantization with our calibration set gives a further 2x memory reduction over fp16

items.label: Auto-fallback:
items.text: if the RKNN runtime is not available or a model conversion fails, the system falls back to CPU ORT

backends.title: QAIRT / QNN
backends.intro: Qualcomm AI Runtime (QAIRT) and the QNN SDK target the Hexagon DSP/NPU and Adreno GPU in Snapdragon-based mini PCs such as the Radxa Dragon Q6A. Delivers maximum efficiency on Qualcomm silicon.

items.label: Hexagon NPU:
items.text: the QAIRT backend routes int8 models to the Hexagon DSP for the lowest power and latency

items.label: Adreno GPU path:
items.text: fp16 models run on the Adreno GPU via the QNN GPU backend when Hexagon is unavailable

items.label: QAT int8:
items.text: int8 models produced by Polaris's own Quantization-Aware Training are the primary target for QAIRT deployment

items.label: Tested on:
items.text: Radxa Dragon Q6A (Snapdragon 865); CPU benchmark score 296, best-value board in our benchmark table

backends.title: CPU Fallback
backends.intro: All models run on CPU via ONNX Runtime when no hardware accelerator is available or selected. No configuration required; performance scales with the number of CPU cores and threads.

items.label: Zero setup:
items.text: ORT CPU is always the last resort; Polaris will always be able to run AI tools regardless of GPU availability

items.label: Multi-threaded:
items.text: ORT uses all available CPU threads for tiled inference; a Raspberry Pi 5 (4 cores) achieves acceptable throughput for light use

items.label: fp32 and fp16:
items.text: CPU backend supports both precision levels; int8 via ORT INT8 quantized operators

items.label: Override:
items.text: you can force CPU in Settings to reproduce a reference result or to leave the GPU free for other workloads

precisionLede: Each AI model ships in multiple precision variants. Polaris's own models are produced using a full training pipeline: fp32 baseline, near-lossless fp16 export, static int16 PTQ, and int8 Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) for artefact-free compression.

precisions.name: fp32
precisions.desc: Full 32-bit floating-point. Largest files, highest memory, used as training baseline and for CPU reference runs.
precisions.detail: All exported models start here. Rarely used in production but essential for verifying that quantized variants are lossless.

precisions.name: fp16
precisions.desc: 16-bit float exported via onnxconverter-common. Essentially lossless vs fp32 (delta less than 0.01 dB PSNR in our evaluations). Roughly 2x smaller. Runs natively on GPU and NPU accelerators.
precisions.detail: Default for ORT Web (WebGPU/WebGL), OpenCL, and RKNN fp16 paths. Best balance of quality, speed, and file size.

precisions.name: int16
precisions.desc: 16-bit integer via static Post-Training Quantization (PTQ). Lossless in practice (within 0.03 dB of fp32). Preferred for RKNN and Qualcomm QNN deployments that want integer arithmetic without int8 accuracy loss.
precisions.detail: QDQ (Quantize-Dequantize) nodes inserted by onnxruntime-tools around every tensor. The calibration set comes from the training data.

precisions.name: int8 (QAT)
precisions.desc: 8-bit integer produced by Quantization-Aware Training: STE fake-quant hooks inserted during fine-tuning so the model learns to compensate for quantization error from the start.
precisions.detail: PTQ int8 showed -3.3 dB PSNR degradation for upscale. QAT brings this back to near-lossless. Halo Removal and Upscaling now ship with QAT models; bge and denoise to follow.
